What we work on

The English your job depends on

This isn’t a general English class. We take the meetings, presentations, emails and conversations you deal with every week and work on saying what you mean, clearly and confidently.

  • Meetings, stand-ups and technical discussions
  • Presentations and client conversations
  • Professional writing, email and documentation
  • Technical and workplace vocabulary
  • Small talk, negotiation and speaking confidence
  • Disagreeing, pushing back and giving feedback
  • Cross-cultural communication

What changes

Small changes in wording make a big difference

We practice language inside situations from your work. Here are a few of the patterns we work on:

Less effectiveMore professional
“I think maybe we could potentially consider changing the approach.”“I recommend changing the approach.”
“Sorry, maybe I didn’t explain this correctly.”“Let me clarify the point.”
“This won’t work.”“I don’t think this approach will work given the current constraints.”
“I just wanted to ask if you maybe had some time to look at this.”“Have you had a chance to review this?”
“I’m not sure, but I think the deadline might be difficult.”“I don’t think we can meet the deadline with the current scope.”
“That’s impossible.”“That isn’t feasible under the current constraints.”
How a session works

Bring something from work and we’ll prepare for it

Each session has a focus you choose: a presentation, an email thread, next week’s meeting or a conversation you keep putting off.

  1. One technique

    I explain one way of structuring what you say, or one piece of language.

  2. Examples

    You hear a strong version and a weak one, and why the difference matters.

  3. Role-play

    We act out your interview, meeting or conversation as realistically as we can.

  4. Feedback

    I tell you exactly what worked and what to change.

  5. Second attempt

    You do it again with the changes. This is where it starts to stick.

  6. One thing to try

    You leave with one thing to use at work before our next session.

Between sessions

Practice between our sessions

A lot of progress happens between sessions. I set everything up with you in the first weeks and we adjust it as you go.

  • A personal learning plan, reviewed and adjusted every month
  • A shared folder with your vocabulary, phrases and resources
  • Flashcards and real examples to help new vocabulary stick
  • Short daily practice for grammar and pronunciation
  • Speaking practice outside sessions, such as Toastmasters
  • A level retest every three months to track progress

Questions

Communication coaching questions

Is this an English course?

Not in the usual sense. We do cover grammar and vocabulary, but through your own meetings, presentations and emails instead of a textbook.

What level do I need?

B1 or above. Business English suits B1–B2 speakers. Executive communication is for C1–C2 speakers who want to sound more confident and persuasive.

Is the first session free?

Yes, and there’s no obligation. We talk about your goals and the situations you want to handle better, and agree on a plan.

How long are packages valid?

Packages of 5 or 10 sessions stay valid for 3 months, and packages of 15, 20 or 25 sessions for 6 months. That’s enough time to use them at a steady pace, even with a busy month or a holiday in between.

Can my employer pay?

Yes. I can give you receipts and invoices for reimbursement.

Where do sessions take place?

Online, on Google Meet. My booking calendar shows the available times in your own time zone.
